newsitem.title: USA: Sallie Mae holder group solicits meeting.
newsitem.headline: Sallie Mae holder group solicits meeting.

text.p: The Committee to Restore Value at Sallie Mae (CRV) said Monday it is asking shareholders of Student Loan Marketing Association (Sallie Mae) to call a special meeting to vote on an alternative plan of reorganization and a new board of directors.

The CRV, which has begun mailing a solicitation statement, said that at the special meeting shareholders would vote on their plan as an alternative to a management-sponsored plan and vote on whom they want as directors of the reorganized company.
The CRV said in a statement it believes that the management plan "unnecessarily strips away basic shareholder rights and fails to include a credible business plan for the future."

It charged that the management plan includes numerous management entrenchment and anti-takeover provisions in the proposed holding company's charter and by-laws and does not provide for a separate shareholder vote on the new holding company's board of directors.

According to the group, a majority of the new holding company board would be individuals who have never been elected by shareholders or who previously were voted off the Sallie Mae board. Also, it said, the new board does not include the eight CRV directors who were elected to Sallie Mae's board in 1995 and were reelected in 1996.

Among the management entrenchment and anti-takeover provisions contained in the management plan are a classified board; elimination of cumulative voting; board authorization to expand the size of the board; poison pills; and supermajority voting provisions, CRV alleged.
It said in addition to proposing an alternative plan, it will nominate a slate of directors that would advocate a business plan for Sallie Mae.
Under Sallie Mae's by-laws, holders of one-third of the outstanding shares can call a special meeting.

Federal legislation that authorizes Sallie Mae to reorganize under a state-chartered holding company requires any plan of reorganization to be approved by shareholders and adopted by the Sallie Mae board before it can become effective.
